A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000, from an error converting $\text{GPa}$ to $\text{Pa}$ or $\text{J m}^{-3}$ to $\text{kJ m}^{-3}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100, from using $0.2 \text{ GPa}$ instead of $2 \text{ GPa}$ or missing a power of 10 in the area calculation.

C.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, often from forgetting the $\frac{1}{2}$ factor is already included and then halving again, or misreading stress as $0.2 \text{ GPa}$.

D.explanation: Equals $\frac{1}{2} \times 2.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Pa} \times 0.010 = 1.0 \times 10^7 \text{ J m}^{-3} = 10 \text{ MJ m}^{-3}$.

hints: Look at the straight line on the stress-strain graph and read the stress in $\text{GPa}$ that corresponds to strain $0.010$ on the horizontal axis.

Recall that strain energy per unit volume is the area under the stress-strain graph, which for a straight line through the origin is the area of a triangle $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}$.

Convert the $2 \text{ GPa}$ stress to $\text{Pa}$ by multiplying by $10^9$, then calculate $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress in Pa} \times 0.010$ and express the $\text{J m}^{-3}$ result in $\text{MJ m}^{-3}$.
walkthrough: Read the graph at strain $= 0.010$. The straight line reaches stress $= 2.0 \text{ GPa}$ on the vertical axis.
State the rule: for elastic deformation, strain energy per unit volume $= $ area under the stress-strain graph $= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}$.
Convert stress to SI units: $2.0 \text{ GPa} = 2.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Pa} = 2.0 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^{-2}$.
Substitute: energy per unit volume $= \frac{1}{2} \times (2.0 \times 10^9) \times 0.010 = 1.0 \times 10^7 \text{ J m}^{-3}$.

Check units: $\text{Pa} \times$ strain (dimensionless) $= \text{N m}^{-2} = \text{J m}^{-3}$, so the result is energy per volume. Convert $1.0 \times 10^7 \text{ J m}^{-3} = 10 \times 10^6 \text{ J m}^{-3} = 10 \text{ MJ m}^{-3}$. This is option D
